heading: Maine Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Maine paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Maine income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable Paid Family and Medical Leave contributions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, choose your payment frequency and customize your payroll deductions to see how much money you could receive on payday.

Maine's income tax system includes progressive tax rates, income-dependent adjustments and paid leave contributions. Understanding these deductions is important when comparing salaries or planning your monthly expenses.

Whether you work in Portland, Bangor, Augusta, Lewiston or another Maine community, this calculator can help you understand the relationship between gross earnings and take-home income.

## How to Use the Maine Paycheck Calculator

Start by selecting whether you receive a fixed annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your earnings before taxes, then select your payment frequency. Enter the federal and Maine income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions and health insurance premiums. If Maine Paid Leave was withheld, enter the amount under Benefits in Advanced settings, under Other deductions.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown and compare it with your latest payroll statement.

Employees with variable earnings, multiple jobs or interstate employment may need to provide additional information to obtain a representative estimate.

## Maine Payroll Taxes in 2026

Maine employees may encounter the following payroll deductions.

Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave

Your actual deductions depend on taxable earnings, withholding information, employment arrangements and employee benefits.

Visit [Maine Revenue Services](https://www.maine.gov/revenue/) for official income tax and employer withholding information.

## How Maine State Income Tax Works

Maine uses a progressive individual income tax system. Its ordinary income tax brackets apply rates of 5.8%, 6.75% and 7.15%, with additional high-income provisions under the revised 2026 rules.

Progressive taxation means that different portions of your taxable earnings may be subject to different rates.

Your highest marginal tax rate should not be applied to your entire gross salary.

Employers calculate withholding using state-approved tables or the authorized percentage method. These calculations account for applicable deductions, withholding allowances and filing classifications.

Maine revised its 2026 withholding instructions during the year to account for increased standard deductions and a new income tax surcharge.

The [revised Maine 2026 withholding instructions](https://www1.maine.gov/revenue/sites/maine.gov.revenue/files/inline-files/26_wh_tab_instr_August2026.pdf) explain the updated methodology.

## Maine Standard Deductions and Personal Exemptions

Maine's revised 2026 guidance identifies a personal exemption amount of $5,300.

The basic annual standard deductions are $15,700 for single filers and $31,400 for married couples filing jointly.

However, these deductions are subject to income-based phase-outs, and the amounts used in the payroll withholding calculation differ slightly from the annual income tax return figures.

Employees should therefore avoid using a simplified annual income tax calculation as a substitute for payroll withholding.

For example, an employee earning $80,000 may have different withholding from another employee earning the same amount because of filing classifications, allowances or additional withholding.

## Understanding Maine Form W-4ME

Maine employees generally use Form W-4ME to provide withholding information to their employers.

The form allows employees to specify applicable withholding allowances, marital classifications and additional withholding amounts.

Your Maine withholding elections are separate from federal Form W-4 information.

Review your withholding certificate when starting a new job, changing your filing status or experiencing a substantial change in household income.

You can obtain current forms through the [Maine Revenue Services tax forms directory](https://www.maine.gov/revenue/tax-return-forms).

Changing your withholding may increase or decrease your immediate take-home pay, but it does not necessarily change your final annual tax liability.

## Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Contributions

Maine's Paid Family and Medical Leave program provides financial benefits to qualifying workers who need time away from employment for eligible family or medical circumstances.

Payroll contributions began in January 2025, and benefits became available in May 2026.

The standard employee share is generally limited to 0.5% of covered wages.

Employers may pay some or all of the employee's contribution.

Assuming the maximum ordinary employee contribution applies and the annual wage limit has not been reached:

parts.caption: Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Contributions

parts.markdown:
The program applies an annual covered wage ceiling corresponding to the Social Security wage base.

For 2026, this ceiling is $184,500, producing a maximum standard employee contribution of $922.50 at the 0.5% rate.

Visit the official [Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave website](https://www.maine.gov/paidleave/) for additional coverage and contribution information.

## Maine Paid Leave Wage Limit Example

Suppose an employee has already earned $183,000 in covered wages and receives another paycheck containing $2,500.

Only $1,500 remains below the annual wage ceiling.

The maximum ordinary employee contribution for this paycheck would be:

$1,500 × 0.005 = $7.50

Applying the contribution rate to the entire paycheck would incorrectly produce a deduction of $12.50.

This illustrates why year-to-date covered wages are an important input for higher-income employees.

Approved private plans and employer-paid contributions may produce different deductions.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Maine Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable earnings, filing status, payroll frequency and Form W-4 information.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages, up to the 2026 annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings without a standard annual wage limit.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when covered Medicare wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

The official calculation procedures are available in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) and the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15).

## Maine Paycheck Example: $65,000 Annual Salary

Suppose you earn $65,000 annually and receive 26 biweekly paychecks.
Assume all wages are subject to ordinary federal payroll contributions and the maximum standard Maine employee paid leave contribution.

Approximately $2,296.25 remains before federal income tax, Maine income tax and other employee deductions.

If your employer pays the entire employee paid leave contribution, the remaining amount would be $12.50 higher under otherwise identical assumptions.

Use your actual withholding amounts to calculate your complete estimated net paycheck.

## Maine Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate their earnings by multiplying their hourly rate by regular working hours and adding qualifying overtime compensation.

Consider an employee earning $26 per hour who works 40 regular hours plus six overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$26 × 40 = $1,040

Overtime earnings:

$26 × 1.5 × 6 = $234

Total gross earnings:

$1,274

At a 0.5% employee paid leave contribution rate, the deduction would be $6.37 if all earnings are covered and the annual limit has not been reached.

Federal and state taxes would also apply.

Consult the [Maine Department of Labor](https://www.maine.gov/labor/) for state employment requirements and overtime guidance.

## Working in Maine and New Hampshire

Employees living near the Maine–New Hampshire border may work in one state while residing in the other.

Although New Hampshire does not impose individual income tax on ordinary wages, working or residing in Maine can still create Maine income tax obligations.

Your employment location, residency and income sourcing determine the appropriate tax treatment.

Remote workers and employees performing duties in multiple states may require more detailed calculations.

A standard Maine paycheck calculator should not be treated as a complete interstate tax estimator.

## Managing Seasonal Earnings in Maine

Tourism, hospitality, fishing and other seasonal industries can produce substantial differences in earnings throughout the year.

Employees may receive higher paychecks during busy months and lower earnings during quieter periods.

When planning your budget, avoid assuming that your highest-paying month represents your normal annual income.

Estimate your total expected earnings and maintain sufficient savings to cover periods of reduced employment.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help you establish a savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare hourly and salaried positions.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Maine's income tax rate in 2026?

Maine's ordinary individual income tax brackets use rates of 5.8%, 6.75% and 7.15%. Revised 2026 rules also include additional high-income provisions. Actual withholding depends on the applicable payroll schedules.

### How much is Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave deducted from paychecks?

Covered employees generally contribute up to 0.5% of eligible wages, subject to the annual wage ceiling of $184,500 in 2026. Employers may cover some or all of the employee contribution.

### Why did my Maine paycheck change during 2026?

Maine issued revised withholding instructions during 2026 to reflect updated deductions and a new income tax surcharge. Changes in federal taxes, benefits and payroll contributions may also affect your earnings.

## Calculate Your Maine Take-Home Pay

The results are educational estimates rather than official payroll calculations or individualized tax advice.
